Standstill with a term. A pause taken to keep an option open is written on an instrument with a term, so a situation that had no deadline acquires one, and the paper's renewal belongs to the counterparty, who now knows what the pause is worth to the holder. The tolling agreement that stops the limitations clock the holder could have stopped alone by filing, and runs out in twelve months unless the adversary signs again; the negotiated leave of absence that dates a job which had no date and is extended only if the employer signs; the forbearance agreement that holds the lender's foreclosure for ninety days; the furlough whose recall rights run six months; the standstill in a takeover that keeps the bidder from buying shares and ends on the day it says. Lost: a permission, the leave to remain in the paused state. Carrier: the pause's own instrument, the only clock in the whole situation the holder wrote with their own hand. Threshold: the instrument's term. Tell: the counterparty has just learned how much this matters to the holder. Changed next move: the renewal asked for before the counterparty learns it is needed, or a pause written without a term, which is rarely granted; the Korean armistice has no renewal date and is still called temporary. Set aside the statutory pauses: the twelve weeks of the family-leave statute and the restraining order's fourteen days are the same date without the mechanism, since the term is a rule's and the renewal belongs to a court or to no one, so the holder gets the deadline without paying the counterparty for it; those are runway-illusions' Stamp's clock. Beside impasse-inventions' cooling-off right, reversibility offered as a chip; this is the bill the chip carries. Not lead-time-floors' No-shop, which serializes the search; here the search is stopped, and the stopping is what expires.
I: Weekend closure. An authority closes an exit by decree on a whole class of holders, and does it in the hours the holders cannot act: Friday night, a bank holiday, after a Sunday address. The timing is structural. An announced closure defeats itself, because the announcement is the signal to run, so the only closure that works is the one nobody was told about. Cases: Greece, the banks that did not open on Monday 29 June 2015 after a Sunday speech; Cyprus, March 2013, a bank holiday stretched past parliament's refusal of the first levy until the bail-in was law; Argentina, the corralito announced on a Saturday in December 2001; an export licence suspended, a delisting printed once it is done. What is lost is a permission, the leave to move what is yours. The clock is the authority's calendar, laid over the hours the holder is locked out. Threshold: the decree itself, which strikes before it can be known; of every expiry on this map this is the one whose notice cannot precede it. Tell: there is none from the authority. The only signal is rumour, and it is priced as rumour, with the discount and the chance of being wrong. The deposits that left Greece that spring left on nothing better than rumour; those who waited for a better reason got a closed door on Monday. Changed next move: transfer on rumour at rumour's price, accepting the error rate. 'I will move when they announce it' is not a plan. Neighbours: runway-illusions' Cash behind glass counts the deposit taken into receivership on a Friday as owned and unreachable; this is the item that chose the Friday. Not investor-tells' Let it lapse, a fuse the founder can test by letting it pass: a closure you can probe is not one that must be a surprise. Not a withdrawn offer or a rival's foreclosure, where somebody at your own table decides; the decree is a rule on a class, and nobody at your table was asked about you. Not a side-effect death: the decree names the exit and forbids it.

Bar date in the newspaper. A claim expires on a date fixed in a proceeding the holder is not attending, and the law deems him to know the date because it was published. Cases: the bankruptcy court's bar date for proofs of claim, noticed to unknown creditors by publication in the county paper between the auction notices; the class settlement whose opt-out date arrives on a postcard dressed as advertising and mailed with the advertising; the probate creditor's window that opens and shuts in the legal-notices column. What is lost is a permission, the standing to be paid or to sue in his own name. The clock is the bar-date order together with the rule of constructive notice, the fiction that publication is knowledge for anyone the debtor could not name. Threshold: the bar date on the docket. Tell: the holder is expecting a letter, and the notice is in a column he does not read. The cure is the cheapest filing in the law, a one-page proof of claim or a signed opt-out, and it is the filing least often made, by construction: the holder who needed to file is exactly the one who was not told. Changed next move: read the legal-notices column and the docket of any proceeding that could name your debtor; file the one page. Neighbours: runway-illusions' Stamp's clock is a permission with a date the holder can read on the stamp; this is the date written on someone else's docket and imputed to him. Not deal-deaths' Missing witness: nothing is missing from the record, the record is complete. The holder is what is missing from the room.

Emergency over. The option was issued under a parent instrument with a term of its own, and it dies when the parent dies, on its merits or not, with no date printed anywhere on the option itself. Cases: the emergency-use authorization, which ends when the declaration it was issued under is terminated, a different paper from the public-health emergency that ended in May 2023 and left the authorizations standing; the cross-state telehealth licence that lapsed state by state with each state's emergency in 2021 and 2022; the wartime power; the pilot programme run under a waiver; the sub-lease that dies with the head lease. What is lost is a permission. The clock is the parent instrument's date, which the holder never signed and, holding a grant with no date on it, had no reason to read. Threshold: the parent's termination. Tell: the grant carries no expiry. That absence is the tell. The first task is not to check the date but to find which parent paper carries it; most holders discover that task exists the morning after. Changed next move: conversion, a full approval, a permanent rule, a licence in one's own name, filed while the parent still stands. Conversion is slow, so it has to begin while the emergency looks endless, which is the week in which beginning it looks unnecessary, which is why it is begun by nobody. Neighbours: not Bar date in the newspaper, where the date is on a docket and imputed; here the date is on a different paper from the option, and it is honest. Not lead-time-floors' Calendar with nothing in it, a wait the rule imposes: this rule does not wait, it ends.

Patch before seven. The option expires by the holder's own development, on a schedule the holder cannot know, so the last intervention is necessarily in another hand. Cases: amblyopia, most correctable by patching the good eye in the first years of life and responding less, and less completely, after about seven, though the trials of the 2000s found response into the early teens; the clubfoot cast in infancy; the second language spoken without an accent, contested as a hard window; the duckling that imprints in its first day. What is lost is a capability, the cortex's willingness to rewire. The clock is the developmental timetable. Threshold: about seven for the eye, with a tail into the early teens. Tell: none from the holder. The child does not know there is an eye to save and will not complain; a plan that waits for the complaint is waiting for a report from a witness who does not know there is anything to report. The tells belong to others: the squint a parent notices, the preschool vision check. Changed next move: screening. The option belongs to one person and its preservation to another, and where there is no screening programme the option expires unseen at a rate that is a property of the programme, not of the child, set by whoever priced the programme and passed. Neighbours: Last known well has a witness dating the option; this is the case where the holder cannot be its own witness at all. Not a use-it-or-lose-it: nothing the child does or leaves undone runs the clock.

Last known well. The protocol dates the option by the last witness to the fact rather than by the fact, so the option expires when the proof runs out while the body might still allow it. Cases: the stroke patient who wakes with the deficit is ineligible for thrombolysis because the four-and-a-half-hour window counts from when she was last seen well, which was bedtime, so the wake-up stroke loses the drug whatever hour the artery closed; the opened vial with no time on the label; the sample whose chain of custody has a gap; each treated as expired at the earliest hour it could have been. What is lost is a capability, a treatment the protocol now forbids. The clock is the protocol's timestamp rule, which asks for a witness and not for the tissue, because a witness is the one thing a chart can hold. Threshold: the window measured from the last witnessed good state, not from onset. Tell: the deficit was found on waking; the label has no time; the custody log has a gap. Changed next move: supply the witness in advance, someone awake, a time written on the vial in the thirty seconds it takes, or supply a witness of another kind, imaging that reads the tissue's own clock, by which the WAKE-UP trial of 2018 returned the drug to patients with no witnessed onset. A unit that owns the scanner and goes on asking the chart is choosing the record's clock over the body's. Neighbours: Witness-architectures asks what must exist for a trace to form; this is the option that dies for want of a trace while the fact would still allow it. Not Patch before seven, where the body's own clock has run. Here the body's clock may not have run at all; the record's has.

Mooted. The option to a decision expires because the situation resolves itself before the forum that would decide it moves, so nobody declines and nobody rules. Cases: DeFunis, 1974, the student whose challenge to a law school's admissions was dismissed as moot because he was about to graduate; the pregnancy over before the appeal; the election held before the ballot-access case; the tenant evicted before the housing court sits; the employee whose grievance is mooted by the reorganization that abolished the post. What is lost is a permission, the justiciability of the claim. The clock is the ratio of the forum's pace to the harm's duration, a number set by no party at the table, which is why pressing on it produces nothing. Threshold: the harm ends before the ruling issues. Tell: the harm's natural duration is shorter than the forum's docket. A motion to expedite does not change the ratio. Changed next move: build a structure that outlives the individual harm. The class certified before the named plaintiff's harm ends, which Sosna, 1975, allowed; or the doctrine that a harm capable of repetition yet evading review may be decided anyway, which is what Roe rested on. The option is kept by a coordination or by a rule and never, in any case on the record, by hurrying. Neighbours: not deal-deaths' Cost of the last mile, where the surplus is eaten along a curve; nothing here is eaten, the harm is simply over. Not Bar date in the newspaper: there is no date anywhere, which is the thing the hurrying lawyer keeps looking for.

Session ends. The body that could have said yes reaches the end of its own term with the matter pending, and its successor never has to say no, because the successor starts the matter at zero. Cases: bills that die on adjournment sine die and must be reintroduced from the beginning; the treaty signed and awaiting a parliament that is dissolved; the permit application before a council that is re-elected; the approval the old board agreed in the corridor and had not yet minuted when the board was reconstituted at the meeting; the offer approved by a committee disbanded in the reorganization. What expires is the matter's place in the process. What is lost is a counterparty, the specific body whose yes was available. The clock is the ratifier's own calendar: election, session, term. Threshold: adjournment, dissolution, reconstitution. Tell: the yes exists only in a corridor and not in a minute, and the matter is still pending as the term runs out; a corridor yes is worth exactly the corridor. Changed next move: the vote scheduled before adjournment, the carry-over motion, the approval minuted rather than agreed in passing. None of it is expensive; all of it requires believing the body will end, which the body's own members are the last to believe. Caveat: the treaty cases are simplified, since most unratified treaties were eventually refused by someone. The clean form is the legislative bill, which dies by the thousand each session with no recorded no; that is not a defeat, there was no enemy. Neighbours: deal-deaths' Ratifier's other deal has a ratifier that wanted a different bargain; this is the ratifier that wanted this one and was gone before the vote. Not Landlord changes, where the counterparty is replaced by transfer; here it is replaced by the calendar.

Landlord changes. An option held in a person rather than on the paper that transfers expires at the counterparty's next transfer, which the holder does not control and often does not see. Cases: the renewal promised by the landlord who sells to a buyer not bound by unrecorded promises; the 'we'll take you back' from a manager who leaves; the side letter with a fund's partner that the fund's successor manager has never seen; the supplier's verbal priority that walks out with the account executive. What is lost is a counterparty, the one whose word held the option. The clock is the register, the deed, the fund agreement, the offer letter on letterhead, on which the option was never written, so the successor takes free of it, and honestly so: the successor owes nothing to a promise he was never shown. Threshold: the transfer. Tell: the promise lives in a relationship and appears on no instrument that binds successors; the reason it was never recorded is that asking felt awkward. Changed next move: record it. A memorandum of option on the title, a side letter countersigned by the entity, the promise put on the paper that binds successors. The cost is one awkward conversation asking a friendly counterparty to bind their unknown replacement, which, held up against the building, is small. Neighbours: term-sheet-powers' Successor in the chair has the replacement exercising a term the friend would not have; this is the mirror, the replacement declining to honour a term the friend gave. Not Chair grown over, where the counterparty stays and the shape goes.

Chair grown over. The option to return rests on a vacancy the counterparty has not yet re-planned, so it expires at the counterparty's next planning cycle without anyone declining the return. Cases: the leave with no return date whose post is redistributed among three people at the next reorganization; the budget line reallocated at year end; the supplier's line retooled for the customer who stayed; the co-founder's seat that the remaining founders stop leaving empty at the next hire. What expires is the return to the seat; employment there afterwards is a new negotiation from the outside. What is lost is a capability on the counterparty's side, the shape that could receive the holder. The clock is the counterparty's planning cadence, quarterly, annual, the next reorganization, which sets the expiry with no reference to the holder at all. Being liked has no entry in a headcount plan. Threshold: the next cycle. Tell: no return date is on file; the seat is being held by goodwill rather than by a reservation the cycle must respect. Changed next move: a dated return, a leave rather than a resignation, a reservation the cycle must honour, or the return itself before the cycle turns. Each is a line on a form; the form goes unfilled because filling it feels like distrust. Neighbours: Traces-of-the-unlived's Vacancy tenant has preparation for a future breeding its own opponents; here no one opposes the return and the absence is simply absorbed. Not forms-of-return's Reentry burn, a road open and hostile one way; this road has closed.

Petition that goes stale. An option that requires many simultaneous yeses expires unless the gathering outruns the decay of each yes, so a coordination has a half-life. Cases: the recall petition whose signatures older than sixty days are void under Michigan's rule, or must all fall within California's hundred and sixty days; the tender offer's minimum condition that must be met by the offer's expiry; the crowd in the square that goes home; the reunion that becomes impossible one death at a time. What is lost is a coordination. The clock is the validity window on each act of assent, written by the rule or by the assenter's own attention, and the attention is the shorter of the two. Threshold: the moment decay outpaces gathering, which shows up at the clerk's counter as the count of still-valid signatures. Tell: the organizer is counting signatures gathered rather than signatures still valid, and the two numbers are diverging by the day. Changed next move: a gathering rate, paid circulators; a date agreed in advance; a pact that binds the early yeses until the last arrives. A drive that will not pay circulators pays anyway, in signatures, at a worse rate. Caveat: the recall and tender cases are observed; the crowd is analogy. Neighbours: Who-can-be-bound's Place in line is an ordering lost by leaving; this is the coordination lost by others' leaving. Not Session ends, where one body's calendar kills the matter; here many small calendars do, and no one of them can be blamed.

Outgrown the buyer. The holder's own growth moves the counterparty out of reach, so the option to sell to the natural acquirer expires at the round that prices the company above what the acquirer can pay at all: a market capitalization smaller than the price, a wage cap, a fund's concentration limit, and past those a board's approval ceiling. Nobody at either table declines. Cases: the company whose preference stack now exceeds the largest deal its three strategic buyers have ever done; the player whose wage outgrows every club in the league but two; the practice too large for any partner to buy in and too small to be listed. What is lost is a counterparty, the buyer whose capacity was the option. The clock is the acquirer's capacity, readable in its market value and its deal history by anyone who looks, set against the holder's own price, which each round raises. Threshold: the round that crosses the ceiling. Tell: compare the preference stack to the acquirer's largest-ever deal before pricing the round; a bigger number is not a better number if it clears the only three balance sheets that could pay it. Changed next move: the sale at the last price under the ceiling, which is never recognised as the last, or a round sized to stay under it, which is the one choice a founder is rarely advised to make, and the advisers' reasons are not the founder's. Caveat: analytical. Every observed case can be read as a buyer that would have paid more, so the item stands as a mechanism and not a count. Neighbours: Market-deaths' Slowed past the rot has a market thinning from the outside; this is the market for the holder that the holder thins by growing. Not Chair grown over, where the counterparty re-plans; here the counterparty is unchanged and the holder has left its range.

Pour the foundation. A permission is about to be withdrawn by a third party's rule change, and it can be kept only by an act in the world that no paper substitutes for. Cases: the building that may proceed under the old zoning only if the developer has substantially begun in reliance on a valid permit before the ordinance passes; the footings poured the week of the council vote; the nonconforming use that survives the new code only if it is in use on the effective date; the grandfathered rate kept only by the account that was open. What is lost is a permission. The clock is the code and the vested-rights doctrine, which in most states vests on construction begun and in a few, Washington among them, on a complete application, so the last act differs by jurisdiction. Threshold: the ordinance's passage or effective date. Tell: the item is on the council's agenda. A lawyer's letter answering the agenda produces a letter; the council produces an ordinance; neither is a building. Changed next move: the hole in the ground before the vote, an exercise begun rather than a filing made, and first, find out which vesting rule your jurisdiction applies, because the holder who knows has a different week from the holder who assumed. Saving the concrete for after the vote saves exactly the concrete. Neighbours: First-mover-forecloses holds the rival who changes the rules on purpose; this is the rule that changes for reasons of its own. Not Slot flown empty, where the exercise must be repeated to keep the right; here one beginning vests it for good.

Slot flown empty. The permission expires by disuse and is kept only by exercise, so the clock runs while the holder does nothing and stops when the holder acts, and the preserving act is the exercise emptied of its purpose. Cases: the airport slot that must be flown eighty percent of the season or returned, which had airlines flying empty aircraft in early 2020 until the rule was waived; the water right under prior appropriation, forfeited after five years without beneficial use, which has fields irrigated in a drought to keep them; the trade mark abandoned after three years' non-use; the mining claim kept by annual labour; the department budget spent in the last quarter so that it is not cut. What is lost is a permission. The clock is the regulator's usage ledger. Threshold: the ledger's figure, eighty percent of the season, five years, three years, the annual labour, the fiscal year end. Tell: the rule is a use-it-or-lose-it, and the ledger is the only thing the regulator reads; empty aircraft are the rule made visible. Changed next move: the empty flight. It costs the whole price of using the option and returns nothing but the option, so keeping and using become the same act and the option's upkeep is its exercise price. Calling that a waste is correct; there is no third choice on offer. Neighbours: runway-illusions' Stamp's clock has a licence that lapses without hours logged and no cash that extends it; this is the price at which it can be extended after all, hours flown for nobody. Tollgates-that-must-buy's Stamp with an expiry has a gate that must spend its stamp; this is the permission-holder who must burn the permission to keep it. Power-trades' Leased strike has disuse making a power unbelieved; this is disuse forfeiting it by rule. Not Pour the foundation, one act that vests; here no act ever finishes the keeping.

Thawed to be ready. Preparing to exercise the option starts a decay the unprepared state did not have, so the option to wait expires because the option to act was made ready. Cases: the vaccine vial that keeps for months frozen, weeks once thawed, hours once punctured; the epoxy whose pot life begins at mixing; the drawn dose; the armed fuze; the reagent brought to room temperature; the opened surgical field; the reserve army that cannot be held at the frontier through the harvest it was drawn from. What is lost is a capability, the good itself spoiling in its ready state. The clock is a chemistry, or a season, that begins at preparation and at nothing else. Threshold: the shelf life of the ready state, hours for a punctured vial, the pot life for the mix. Tell: the whole tray was thawed to be sure of serving whoever came; the certainty was bought with the doses poured out at closing, and on the arithmetic the certainty was the dearer purchase. Changed next move: do not prepare, or prepare in the smallest unit, the single-dose vial, the small mix, the tranche thawed for the day's bookings. Small units are fiddly; that objection weighs a fiddle against a tray. Neighbours: the mirror of Slot flown empty, where the option dies of not being touched. Here it dies of being touched, and a holder who holds both must burn the one and refrain from readying the other; one rule applied to both buys the wrong outcome on one of them. Not lead-time-floors' Understudy, a finished copy waiting, since the understudy does not spoil for having been rehearsed. Not Kept on the machine, where the harm falls on the holder and is billed by the day; here it falls on the good.

First or never. The option must be taken before any other move on a linked matter, so its clock is the holder's own next act rather than a date. A holder who does nothing keeps it; a holder who does anything adjacent loses it. Cases: the objection to the court's jurisdiction over the defendant, waived if left out of the first response; the patent dead in Europe on the morning of the conference talk and a year later in the United States; the appeal waived by accepting the settlement; the election of remedies; the defect in the goods that must be objected to before the goods are used; the 'speak now' at the wedding. What is lost is a permission. The clock is a rule that binds the option to a position in a sequence, and the sequence is written somewhere other than the option: the rules of procedure, the patent statute, the sales code. Threshold: the first adjacent act, the talk given, the answer filed on the merits, the goods unpacked. Tell: there is none on the option itself; the order is learned from the rulebook in advance or from the loss afterwards. The inventor who talked on Monday and called the attorney on Tuesday has, in Europe, a well-attended talk and nothing else. Changed next move: the ordering itself. The provisional application filed the morning of the talk, the reservation written into the first filing, the objection lodged before the goods are unpacked. Each costs nothing but the knowledge that an order exists, and strong merits answered out of turn are worth nothing. Neighbours: not Slot flown empty, where the holder's inaction runs the clock; here inaction is the only thing that keeps it. Not Bar date in the newspaper: there is no date, and the holder is the only one who can strike.

Rollback horizon. The option to reverse a move expires at the first act the new state performs that the old state cannot read, so the window is the gap between the change and its first consequence, and it closes without anyone deciding to close it. Cases: the migration that can be rolled back until the new service writes its first record in a shape the old schema rejects; the merger reversible until the first combined payroll; the new address reversible until the first piece of mail arrives there; the reorganization reversible until the first hire is made into the new chart; the currency changeover until the first contract is written in the new unit. What is lost is a capability, the old state's ability to take over from here. The clock is the first write, performed by the new state in the ordinary course and not as a decision about the reversal at all. Threshold: the first write. Tell: 'we can always roll back' is true only for the length of the pause between the cutover and the first write, and a go/no-go meeting booked for Friday is booked for a window the Tuesday batch job already closed. Changed next move: the expand-and-contract shape, writing to both for a season so the old can still read, at the price of running two and of a season in which neither is the truth; and the go/no-go scheduled before the first write, not after. Declining the dual-write as overhead means paying for it later as a rewrite. Neighbours: Pivot-invariants names the retained assets that make leaving cheap; this is the moment one of them is lost. Undo-costs bills a reversal that remains possible; this is the reversal that stops being possible, and no bill is issued. Not Thawed to be ready, where readiness spoils the good; here the new state's use closes the way back to the old.

Kept on the machine. The option is held open by a device or an upkeep whose own running accumulates a harm or whose lapse is one-way, so the deadline is the machine's and not the situation's. Cases: the patient on ECMO as a bridge to transplant who becomes ineligible for the transplant the machine was keeping her alive for, since bleeding, infection, and clotting rise with each week on circuit and centres set a duration beyond which candidacy is reviewed; the mothballed mine kept dry by pumps whose stopping floods the workings past reopening; the ship in the reserve fleet whose hull is kept by cathodic protection that a budget line can end; the interim chief who has run the company past the point where the search can bring in an outsider. What is lost is a capability, the eligibility or the workings. The clock is the bridge itself, its complication rate or its upkeep bill. Threshold: the centre's duration limit, the budget line's end, the point past which the search cannot land an outsider. Tell: the bridge is holding, and that fact is being read as time bought. It says nothing about the deadline; the time is billed at the bridge's rate, not the situation's. Changed next move: a listing at the moment of cannulation, a search begun the day the interim was named, a decision to stop pumping taken while a sale was still possible. Each treats the bridge's start as the option's deadline. Caveat: the ECMO limits are centre practice and are simplified; claim no more precision than the centres have. Neighbours: Lead-time-floors' Bridge is a degraded replacement priced by the hour; this is the bridge that ends the option it holds open. Not Standstill with a term, where the clock is a date the counterparty signs; here the clock is a harm nobody signs.

Standstill with a term. A pause taken to keep an option open is written on a paper with a date, so a situation that had no deadline acquires one, and the paper's renewal belongs to the counterparty, who now knows what the pause is worth to the holder. Cases: the tolling agreement that stops the limitations clock and expires in twelve months unless the adversary signs again; the negotiated leave of absence that dates a job which had no date and is extended only if the employer signs; the forbearance agreement that holds the lender's foreclosure for ninety days; the furlough whose recall rights run six months; the standstill in a takeover that keeps the bidder from buying shares and ends on the day it says. What is lost is a permission, the leave to remain in the paused state. The clock is the pause's own instrument, the only clock in the situation that the holder wrote. Threshold: the term on the paper. Tell: the one deadline in the room is the one the holder drafted, and its renewal is the counterparty's to sell at a price the counterparty now knows the holder will pay. The plaintiff who tolled to spare himself the cost of filing stopped a clock he could have stopped alone, by filing. Changed next move: the renewal asked for before the counterparty learns it is needed; a pause written without a term, which is rarely granted (the Korean armistice is the exception with no renewal date, and is still called temporary); or the filing itself, where the holder can stop the clock unaided. Caveat: the statutory pauses, the twelve weeks of the family-leave statute and the restraining order's fourteen days, are the same date without the mechanism, since the term is a rule's and the renewal belongs to a court or to no one; those are runway-illusions' Stamp's clock. Neighbours: Impasse-inventions' cooling-off right offers reversibility as a chip; this is the bill the chip carries. Not lead-time-floors' No-shop, which serializes the search; here the search is stopped, and the stopping is what expires.
